title: We also
instructions: pickled our souse --cutting it in thin slices, and laying them in strong vinegar an hour before serving. Another way was to melt the souse into a sort of rich hash--beaten eggs were occasionally added, and the result served on hot toast.  At a pinch it answered for the foundation of a

putting in with it in layers, sliced hard boiled eggs, sliced cucumber pickle, plenty of seasoning, a good lump of butter, and a little water. The pie was baked quickly--and made a very good supper dish if unexpected company overran the supply of sausage or chicken for frying.
